episode.title: Move curated model-picker metadata to a remotely refreshable catalog with resilient local fallbacks
episode.before: At parent d09ab8ff13329da1715d20e3fb17d47f499fbc18, curated model identifiers and descriptions were compiled into the CLI. OpenRouter selection began from OPENROUTER_MODELS before applying live availability, tool-support, and pricing filters; Nous model and authentication flows read _PROVIDER_MODELS["nous"] directly. Updating either curated list therefore required changing and releasing the CLI, and there was no versioned remote catalog, catalog cache, schema validation, or provider-specific catalog override.
episode.after: At 855366909f659e7f11635dc5bfbd279a1d4ef83e, a versioned JSON manifest published with the documentation site carries curated provider/model metadata. A configurable runtime resolver validates remote manifests, uses fresh disk and in-process caches, refreshes stale data, accepts provider-specific override URLs, and degrades through stale cache to bundled snapshots without raising to picker callers. Existing picker behavior is preserved: OpenRouter still applies live tool-support and pricing filtering to the resolved curated identifiers, while Nous selection and authentication flows consume a helper that always returns either remote or bundled model identifiers.
episode.diff: The commit adds hermes_cli/model_catalog.py for configuration, HTTP retrieval, minimum schema validation, atomic disk caching, TTL handling, overrides, provider-shaped accessors, and cache reset; adds model_catalog defaults to hermes_cli/config.py; adds a published manifest and generator; changes hermes_cli/models.py to resolve remote curation before bundled lists; routes the Nous model and login flows through the new resolver; and adds 21 focused tests covering schema rejection, caching, refresh, failures, stale-cache recovery, disabled operation, overrides, accessors, and bundled-list integration fallbacks. Documentation and sidebar entries describe the contract and operational behavior.

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, fetch_openrouter_models copied OPENROUTER_MODELS directly, and the Nous model-selection and login flows obtained model identifiers directly from _PROVIDER_MODELS["nous"].
evidence_units.source: git show d09ab8ff13329da1715d20e3fb17d47f499fbc18:hermes_cli/models.py (fetch_openrouter_models); git show d09ab8ff13329da1715d20e3fb17d47f499fbc18:hermes_cli/main.py (_model_flow_nous); git show d09ab8ff13329da1715d20e3fb17d47f499fbc18:hermes_cli/auth.py (_login_nous)

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit states that curated OpenRouter and Nous picker lists now resolve through a hosted JSON manifest, with cache and bundled-list fallbacks so lists can change without a CLI release.

The change adds a schema-versioned manifest with provider blocks, model identifiers, optional descriptions, and free-form metadata, plus a generator that converts the bundled curated lists into that format.
The default configuration enables remote catalog resolution, defines the master URL and 24-hour TTL, and provides a map for per-provider URL overrides.

The catalog loader rejects non-object manifests, missing or unsupported versions, malformed provider blocks, non-list model collections, and model entries without non-empty string identifiers; HTTP, decoding, validation, and I/O failures return no remote manifest instead of escaping to callers.

Catalog resolution uses a fresh disk-backed in-process cache when possible, fetches when forced or stale, writes fetched data through a temporary file and os.replace, returns stale validated disk data after fetch failure, and otherwise returns an empty catalog for higher-level bundled fallback.

Provider resolution optionally fetches a provider-specific manifest first, falls back to the master catalog, and adapts provider blocks into the pre-existing OpenRouter tuple shape or Nous identifier-list shape; empty or unavailable data is represented as None.

OpenRouter now uses remotely resolved tuples when available and otherwise OPENROUTER_MODELS, then retains its existing live availability, tool-capability, pricing, and recommended-model processing. The Nous adapter similarly returns remote identifiers when non-empty and otherwise a copy of the bundled list.

Both the interactive Nous model flow and the Nous authentication flow were changed from direct bundled-map access to get_curated_nous_model_ids, so they share the same remote-to-bundled resolution behavior.
Focused tests accept a valid manifest and reject invalid top-level values, missing versions, future versions, missing providers, empty identifiers, and non-string identifiers.

Focused tests prove fetched manifests are persisted, ordinary repeated calls avoid another fetch, forced refresh refetches, no-cache failure returns an empty catalog, and both fresh and stale disk data survive network failure.

Focused tests prove provider accessors preserve their expected result shapes, missing catalogs return None, disabled configuration avoids network access, an override takes precedence, and the Nous public helper prefers manifest data while falling back to its bundled snapshot.

candidate_atomics.name: define-versioned-capability-catalog
candidate_atomics.title: Define a versioned catalog for curated capability metadata
candidate_atomics.description: Represent remotely changeable curated identifiers and annotations in a versioned, provider-partitioned manifest while retaining bundled snapshots as an independent fallback.

semantic_action.intent: Allow curated model-picker metadata to be updated independently of application releases without removing the installed fallback dataset.
semantic_action.pre_state: Curated identifiers and descriptions exist only in application code and require a release to change.
semantic_action.post_state: A published, schema-versioned manifest carries provider-partitioned identifiers and annotations, and the application still ships equivalent fallback lists.
semantic_action.validation: Generate or inspect the manifest and verify that it has the supported version, provider model arrays, non-empty identifiers, and the consumer-required optional annotations.

candidate_atomics.name: validate-external-catalog-contract
candidate_atomics.title: Reject incompatible catalog data before use
candidate_atomics.description: Validate the minimum structural contract of externally supplied catalog data and convert retrieval or contract failures into an unavailable result.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent malformed or future-incompatible remote metadata from entering model-selection behavior.
semantic_action.pre_state: An HTTP response or cached object is untrusted and may have an unsupported version or malformed provider/model structure.
semantic_action.post_state: Only manifests with a supported integer version, provider mapping, model arrays, and non-empty string identifiers are admitted; invalid input is treated as unavailable.
semantic_action.validation: Run valid- and invalid-manifest cases covering top-level type, version presence and support, provider structure, and identifier type and emptiness.

candidate_atomics.name: resolve-catalog-with-cache-fallbacks
candidate_atomics.title: Resolve remote metadata through a bounded cache and fallback ladder
candidate_atomics.description: Choose fresh cached data when valid, refresh stale or forced data, persist successful responses atomically, and retain stale validated data after network failure.

semantic_action.intent: Keep catalog-backed features responsive and usable across repeated calls, offline operation, and remote service failures.
semantic_action.pre_state: Remote catalog availability is uncertain, and local cache data may be absent, fresh, or stale.
semantic_action.post_state: The resolver returns validated fresh or stale catalog data when available, performs refresh according to TTL or force policy, and returns an empty result rather than raising when no catalog source succeeds.
semantic_action.validation: Verify persistence after successful fetch, no redundant fetch for a fresh cache, forced refetch, stale-cache recovery, and empty-result behavior with neither network nor cache.

candidate_atomics.name: adapt-provider-catalog-shapes
candidate_atomics.title: Adapt provider catalog entries to stable consumer shapes
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve optional provider-specific sources and map generic provider blocks into the tuple or identifier-list shapes expected by existing consumers.

semantic_action.intent: Introduce a generic manifest without forcing existing consumers to understand its storage schema.
semantic_action.pre_state: Consumers require provider-specific collection shapes, while remote metadata uses a shared provider-block schema and may be unavailable or overridden.
semantic_action.post_state: Each provider accessor returns its established collection shape from an override or master catalog, or a clear unavailable result that activates higher-level fallback.
semantic_action.validation: Verify exact tuple and identifier-list outputs, empty-catalog None results, disabled-network behavior, and provider-override precedence.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-dynamic-curation-with-picker-invariants
candidate_atomics.title: Use dynamic curation without weakening picker invariants
candidate_atomics.description: Substitute remotely curated identifiers at the existing selection boundary while preserving bundled fallback and any live capability, availability, pricing, or access checks.

semantic_action.intent: Make picker membership remotely refreshable while preserving the safety and UX rules already applied by downstream selection flows.
semantic_action.pre_state: Picker consumers read bundled lists directly or begin live filtering from a fixed compiled list.
semantic_action.post_state: Picker consumers begin from remote curation when usable, fall back to bundled curation otherwise, and continue applying their existing live capability, pricing, availability, and access logic.
semantic_action.validation: Verify manifest preference and bundled fallback through the public helper, then exercise affected selection flows to confirm their downstream filtering and tier logic remain in place.

candidate_workflows.name: externalize-curated-capability-metadata-safely
candidate_workflows.title: Externalize curated capability metadata without making selection depend on the network
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for moving release-bound model curation into a remotely refreshable catalog while retaining contract validation, bounded caching, bundled recovery, stable consumer shapes, and existing picker capability checks.

workflow_graph.goal: Make curated model and capability metadata independently refreshable while guaranteeing that invalid data, network loss, or hosting failure cannot break model selection or bypass existing eligibility checks.
when_to_use: Curated model or capability lists change more frequently than application releases.
Consumers already have bundled curated defaults that can serve as a safe last-resort snapshot.
Remote metadata can be separated from live capability, pricing, availability, or authorization data and reconciled at a defined selection boundary.
anti_goals: Do not make the remote catalog the sole source required for the picker to function.
Do not move volatile pricing, context limits, availability, authorization, or other live provider facts into a slowly cached curation manifest.
Do not bypass existing capability, pricing, tier, or availability filters merely because an identifier appears in the remote catalog.
Do not expose the generic manifest representation directly to consumers that already depend on stable provider-specific result shapes.
not_applicable_when: No trustworthy bundled or cached fallback can satisfy offline operation.
The metadata is authoritative live state that must never be stale, such as current authorization or real-time availability.
Consumers cannot identify a compatibility boundary where remote entries can be validated and adapted before use.
inputs: Existing bundled curated collections and their consumer-facing shapes
A supported manifest schema version and provider/model field contract
Remote publication URL, refresh TTL, timeout, cache path, and optional provider overrides
Existing selection-time capability, availability, pricing, and access checks
Failure and compatibility cases for focused tests
workflow_graph.entry_state: Curated picker membership is compiled into the application, consumers may access those collections directly, and no validated remote refresh or cache/fallback policy exists.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Consumers can receive updated curation from a validated remote catalog, but fresh or stale caches and bundled snapshots preserve operation during failure, while established selection-time eligibility rules remain authoritative.

steps.condition: Remote curation must have an explicit compatibility contract and an installed fallback representation.
steps.validation: Inspect or generate a manifest whose supported version, provider blocks, identifiers, and optional annotations correspond to the bundled curated collections.

steps.condition: All remote and cached payloads cross an untrusted metadata boundary.
steps.validation: Valid fixtures are admitted and malformed types, versions, provider blocks, arrays, and identifiers are rejected.

steps.condition: The feature must remain usable across latency, offline operation, invalid responses, and hosting failures.
steps.validation: Successful fetch persists data; fresh cache suppresses fetch; forced or stale access refreshes; failed refresh retains validated stale data; total catalog failure returns an empty result without raising.

steps.condition: Provider consumers require stable shapes or optional provider-specific catalog sources.
steps.validation: Provider accessors return exact expected shapes, overrides take precedence when valid, and unavailable or disabled catalogs produce the documented fallback signal.

steps.condition: Existing picker and authentication consumers must adopt remote curation without changing downstream eligibility semantics.
steps.validation: Public selection helpers prefer usable manifest entries, fall back to bundled entries, and retain existing live tool-support, pricing, availability, and tier checks.

validation_ladder: Contract level: accept the supported manifest and reject incompatible versions and malformed provider/model entries.
Resolution level: prove persistence, fresh-cache reuse, forced refresh, and stale-cache recovery after network failure.
Adaptation level: prove stable provider-specific output shapes, disabled behavior, and override precedence.
Integration level: prove public helpers prefer remote curation and return bundled snapshots when the catalog is unavailable.
Consumer level: exercise model and authentication flows to confirm existing live capability, pricing, availability, and access checks remain authoritative.
stop_conditions: Stop if no bundled or otherwise trustworthy fallback exists and offline operation is required.
Stop if malformed or unsupported catalog data can reach selection consumers without rejection.
Stop if a fetch or cache failure can raise through the picker instead of producing a fallback result.
Stop if adopting remote identifiers removes or bypasses existing live eligibility checks.
Defer promotion as fully runtime-validated when the focused tests cannot be executed in the available environment.
unresolved_or_deferred: The committed focused tests were inspected but not executed because pytest is absent from the available Python environment.
The issue bundle contains no PR discussion, reviews, or recorded status-check results.

No end-to-end interactive picker or authentication-flow test was added in this change; direct consumer routing is established from the diff, while automated integration coverage stops at the model helper.

unresolved_questions: Did CI execute and pass the 21 focused tests? The supplied GitHub bundle contains no status checks, and local execution was unavailable because pytest is not installed.

The validator accepts integer schema versions less than or equal to 1 rather than explicitly requiring version 1; tests cover missing and future versions but not zero or negative versions, so intended backward-version semantics are not fully established.

Provider-specific override fetches intentionally bypass disk caching and run on each accessor call; the evidence does not establish whether this latency tradeoff received production or end-to-end validation.
